doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Playing with Cuban Bennett in Earl Hines's Pittsburgh sextet
summary: Carter played baritone with Cuban in Earl Hines's sextet in 1925 and describes him as easygoing and quietly funny.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Okay, well, if anything else occurs. I think Cuban Bennett’s name will come up again. Well, maybe we should deal with that now. Did you play with him in Pittsburgh [Pennsylvania], with Earl Hines?

Oh yes. Yes, I did play with him in Pittsburgh, but not after he came to New York. Yes, that was in 1925. Earl Hines had a sextet in which I played baritone saxophone. Yes, yes, Cuban was in that, but after he came to New York . . .
So that was the only time you worked professionally with him in any capacity?
That’s the only time I remember, you know.
What was he like personally? I mean, was he difficult to get along with or . . .
Very easygoing, very easygoing. Never difficult to get along with. A rather quiet personality and a great sense of humor. No, he wasn’t difficult to get along with at all.
Did he realize that he was doing anything out of the ordinary as a musician, or was he . . .

I don’t think he did. I think he just enjoyed it, and that was it. But, see, he was from a family that they all played something, almost all of them, you know. But he was especially gifted. He was a very nice guy, yeah.
